knowledge_gaps: The negative sampler requires user identities, but the specified loader returns (None, sequence, positive, negative). Truncated sequences cannot reliably identify users or recover complete histories. Specify an aligned user-ID side channel without changing the required loader output.

The loss is underspecified: define temperature, duplicate-negative handling, position weighting, and whether the objective is candidate-set cross-entropy or an approximation to full-catalog softmax. Uniform sampling over a user-dependent exclusion set does not automatically resolve correction for a deterministically included positive.

The residual adds recent features while retaining the entire SASRec state, so it does not explicitly suppress stale influence. Compare against gated interpolation and loss-only training. Gate bias −2 also does not ensure a small initial perturbation unless feature scales and initialization are controlled.

Reproduction requires optimizer settings, pooling masks and normalization, checkpoint selection, validation frequency, and a concrete GPU-budget allocation. Chunked backward passes through shared sequence features require an explicit graph-retention or recomputation strategy; otherwise they may fail or retain substantial memory.

Diagnostic comparisons need fixed sampled positions and negatives, evaluation mode, and embedding/logit scale measurements. Absolute margins can increase through score scaling without improving ranking; mean cosine similarity alone cannot rule out other forms of representation collapse.

Repeated selection on 200 validation users per category risks validation overfitting. Predeclare a small comparison schedule and report paired uncertainty. Originality is incremental, potential remains speculative, and difficulty is understated until sampler integration and memory management are resolved.
